items.text: Sign-ups are the one fragile check: 0.8 subscribers per 1,000 views in the latest read, which comes from an older finished episode, against a usual 1.8. The direction is softening.
items.recommendation: Add one spoken subscribe ask at the busiest point of the next live and repeat it in a pinned comment. Then compare sign-ups with the last few episodes to see whether the ask moves anything.

items.text: E13, still in its first weeks, gave DesignerTom 8 subscribers at 4.2 per 1,000 views and Dive Club 3 at 1.1 per 1,000. It is an early read, not comparable with finished episodes.
items.recommendation: Write down how each channel presents its subscribe prompt, then copy the stronger version onto the weaker channel for one episode and re-check the per-channel sign-ups.

items.text: Two episodes still in their first weeks lost viewers early, about 7 minutes in: E12 lost 3.7 of every 100 during off-topic chat, E13 lost 3.3 during an install how-to.
items.recommendation: Next episode, push housekeeping and install asks later and open with the first guest or demo. Then check whether the loss around 7 minutes in shrinks. Treat it as a test, not a certain fix.

items.text: Search and suggested videos made up a 7.6 share of YouTube views in the latest read, from an older finished episode, against a usual 14.3. Announce-to-play is 22.8 against a usual 26.2.
items.recommendation: Rewrite the next two episode titles and descriptions around the guest name and the tool people would search. Post each announce with a short clip instead of text alone, and compare both numbers next week.

items.text: Live turnout and chat are healthy: 79.6 chatters per 100 viewers against a usual 53.9, and 113 average live viewers against a usual 74. This is the strength to protect.
items.recommendation: Keep the newest episode's live format, guest mix and chat prompts for the next show. Note which segments drew the most chat before changing any of them.
